title: Rate regression on overdispersed counts with unequal follow-up
summary: Estimates an incidence rate ratio from counts with an offset for person-time, with standard errors that survive overdispersion.
_clustering_is_a_different_entry: clustered is false above. A robust sandwich standard error here corrects for the variance not matching the mean and still assumes patients are INDEPENDENT. Where patients share a ward or clinic, or where one patient contributes several rows, the correction has to be BY CLUSTER and this entry must not be routed to such a plan.
pinned_defaults: R: offset(log(person_time)) INSIDE the formula, which fixes the coefficient at 1. Writing + log(person_time) instead estimates it, and the model runs.
Python: offset=np.log(person_time), already logged, the same convention as R and SAS.
SAS: offset=log_pt, a variable that must ALREADY be logged; the data step does it explicitly.

Stata: exposure(person_time) -- STATA IS THE ODD ONE OUT. exposure() takes the person-time itself and logs it; offset() takes the log. A file translated from any of the other three by swapping the keyword fits exp(person_time) where person_time belongs, runs, converges and answers a different question.
R: vcovHC(type = "HC0"). Python: cov_type="HC0". Stata: vce(robust). SAS: a REPEATED statement with type=ind, which is what asks GENMOD for empirical rather than model-based errors.

The negative binomial dispersion is reported as ALPHA in every file. R's glm.nb reports THETA, which is its reciprocal, and the R file converts rather than emitting a differently scaled number under the same name.
